Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How do I become successful at maintaining friendships?
Answer: By maintaining them, of course, Silly! Invest time in contacting them. Be interested in their lives, and include them in your activities and social circle whenever possible. Share your resources with them on par with how they share with you. Living close enough to each other to frequently be physically present together is a major factor in maintaining friendships. Likewise, any time one friend moves into a new situation more distant is likely to be a major factor in declining friendship quality and requires more effort to maintain.

Question: What is your definition of friends?
Answer: I’m a Christian, so this 1977 song written by a New Zealander about the relationship of friends has references to that. However, it expresses the idea of friends being faithful, honest, helpful and long-lasting in the lines, “We are here to help each other, Walk the miles and bear the load.” That’s my definition of friendship. “The Servant Song” Brother, sister, let me serve you; Let me be as Christ to you; Pray that I might have the grace to Let you be my servant, too. We are pilgrims on a journey; We are family on the road; We are here to help each other Walk the miles and bear the load. I will hold the Christ-light for you In the nighttime of your fear; I will hold my hand out to you, Speak the peace you long to hear. I will weep when you are weeping; When you laugh I’ll laugh with you; I will share your joys and sorrows Till we’ve seen this journey through. When we sing to God in Heaven We shall find such harmony, Born of all we’ve known together Of Christ’s love and agony. Brother, sister, let me serve you; Let me be as Christ to you; Pray that I might have the grace to Let you be my servant, too. By Richard Gillard

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: I have no friends despite talking to lots of people, having fun with them, and asking them questions. Everyone sees me as an acquaintance. What is wrong with me?
Answer: Nothing is wrong with you OR them. You all are acquaintances — know each other’s names, something about them and talk to each other. All of that is just normal social pastimes. You were in a crowd with them and that was it. Nobody actually helped anybody so there are no favors, no kindnesses to repay to attach you to anyone, and no time together while you share a common interest more deeply. The first two stanzas of the Christian “The Servant Song” say, “Will you let me be your servant, Let me be as Christ to you; Pray that I may have the grace to Let you be my servant, too. We are pilgrims on a journey, We are travelers on the road; We are here to help each other, Walk the mile and bear the load.” You have to do something with someone to reach the time to share more deeply with an individual and open up to each other.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: It bothers me when family and friends that I invite to my home, don't invite me to their home. I know they have excuses, but it prolongs the mismatch. How do you handle it in your own life?
Answer: Let me start by saying, every large “family of families” that sticks together through a generation or two has someone or more who provide the glue for the sticking. They are the ones who make the arrangements for it to happen. They are also the ones whose hospitality makes memorable, those times. And, they will be the ones most remembered and missed by the largest attendance at their funerals. Think on that. In our extended family of about 40 who will attend a get-together at Easter, Thanksgiving, and Christmas, we have one family who graciously hosts us in their small home. It is our branch of the family’s ancestral home and we’ll bring more than enough food, drinks, ice, paper goods and utensils, etc., and folding chairs. Outside are a basketball goal and usually a volleyball net while inside are the conversationalists and ESPN lovers in the living room. When the crowd thins out after about 4–5 hours, whoever is left helps in the general cleanup and putting back folding chairs in the attic. Usually in August, my wife and I will host a get-together at our rural home in the National Forest. Our living room holds six recliners, a table for four and a big screen. The dining room will seat ten but most will bask outside in the shade or go fishing or swimming in our lake. I’ll usually grill burgers and such, and lots of folks bring food, drinks, ice, and picnic tableware. Freezers of homemade ice cream (my wife’s speciality are peach and Butterfinger) will join other desserts. That’s how we handle it. And by the way, everybody hugs everybody coming and going because we love each other and glad for the get-together.

Question: Is it important for you to carry a gun when you leave your house?

I live in the edge of a National Forest, and last week I picked up a non-poisonous snake beside my truck door. I freed it in the woods, but we have killed poisonous ones as close as our back door and front walkway, and since our house on the hill is surrounded on three sides by a lake, we encounter all sorts of animals and reptiles; some dangerous. And when we do leave our home, we usually have to travel some distance through long stretches between towns. Our nearest metropolitan area is Memphis TN USA which has the highest crime rate in the nation. Carjackings and murders, drive-by shootings and other violent crimes top the list. I believe it’s only being wise to prepare at least a semblance of ability to defend our lives.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: How do you get your current friends to ask you to hang out on weekends without initiating contact first?
Answer: Your question is like, “How do you go swimming without first getting in the water?” You can’t. I sense that you aren’t really close with those you call friends. Perhaps you are new to the group, or you fear rejection and for whatever reason, haven’t really joined them in their activities. It sounds like you are an acquaintance on the fringe of the group, on the outside looking in. It’s up to you to overcome your fears of rejection to break the barrier between yourself and them. I had a friend who embodied this old joke: “A man walked up to a woman at an open party. After briefly exchanging names he boldly asked, ‘Do you want to f**k?’ Insulted, she slapped him and walked away. But later, she returned and asked him if that was his usual pick-up line, and he agreed that it was. She responded, ‘Then I’ll bet you get slapped a lot.’ He replied, ‘Yes, I do. But I also get to f**k a lot also.’” You may get rejected a lot, but but you can’t really join the group if you don’t ask. And if all you get is rejections, then you’ll learn that they aren’t really your friends, and you’ll be free to find another group.

Question: What fun hobbies I can do to meet new people?

I saw a couple of children in your photos, apparently a boy and a girl. So, their genders only matter when it comes to the gender of their teams when playing sports like baseball or softball, soccer and other sports in school or recreational league activities. My wife and I have spent most Monday nights for five years, attending our Autistic granddaughter’s Special Needs Athletics softball or basketball games. That was over ten years ago and one of her handicapped teammates exchanges messages with me often. Her younger sister played with her back then, and for the last eight years we have followed her softball games from Rec leagues to “Travel Ball” tournaments and school varsity softball and basketball games. I’ve been involved in the Christian growth events, “Emmaus Walk” and “Cursillo,” the latter of which is the most clean fun. Lots of play and hugging in that one. One of my hobbies is crafting small items like crosses and such, usually from whitetail deer antlers. I make unique walking canes and staffs from saplings in the woods around our home. I make friends with other crafters at farmers markets and craft shows. Hopefully all of this will get you off your duff and onto the trail of making new friends!

Question: Today when my friends and I were walking we were suddenly surrounded by 8 thieves and I ran away from my friends and was I right?
Answer: “WE WERE,” You said, so your friends had the same chance to run. You were right to run away from the thieves, protecting yourself from loss and danger. Hopefully the others were as smart and as fast as you were. Surely no one could fault you for not standing there to hand over your goods, and you don’t owe them anything. Stewardesses on airline flights instruct the passengers that in case of an in-flight emergency and the air masks drop down, they should put their own on first before trying to help others with theirs. Otherwise, they might pass out and be useless and everybody dies. Firefighters may act carelessly around fires, but I was taught as a fireman, “Never walk into a fire that you aren’t certain you can walk out of.” I won’t do it again. Always be sure you can save yourself before you try saving others in an apparently hopeless situation.

Question: Is it normal that if someone made you so furious and you cannot do anything except can't stop talking about the maltreatment to your friends as a way to "let it out" for months?

(Ephesians 4:31-32 NRSV) Forgiveness is not foolishness. Forgiveness is, at its core, choosing to see your offender with different eyes. When some Moravian missionaries took the message of God to the Eskimos, the missionaries struggled to find a word in the native language for forgiveness. They finally landed on this cumbersome twenty-four-letter choice: issumagijoujungnainermik. You don’t excuse him, endorse her, or embrace them. You just route thoughts about them through heaven. -- Max Lucado in “Facing Your Giants”

Question: Has anyone ever gotten a FB friend Request from a dead friend? (I just did.)

And I’ve gotten repeated requests from several deceased friends, probably because nobody is managing their accounts. My Fb account shows that I have 826 “Fb friends.” Some are truly my offline friends, some are online-only friends, some I became acquainted with in spiritual growth programs like Cursillo and Walk to Emmaus, some I met who were members of churches I served, and there are some who were attracted by my theology or other interests. Nowadays when I receive Fb friend requests, I go to the applicant’s page and if it doesn’t look like a legitimate request from a real, living friend, I notify Fb that it’s a scam and delete the request.

Question: Why do some people claim to have no friends but still have a large social circle? Is this statement true or do they actually have friends?
Answer: “Friends” is a rather flexible term for others you know besides family. I’m a church pastor, and I have met and been in company with literally thousands of people in my life. Some became friends while I served in their churches, and besides church attendance we did the things friends do to help each other. Friends usually can maintain contact with each other even if they don’t live close enough to exchange help or do things together. I also came to become acquainted with many others in those communities. We knew each other’s names, family members, phone numbers, etc., saw each other once or more times a month and were friendly with each other in social settings. Such people are often loosely called ‘friends’ because they can become more useful to us, but they are actually ‘acquaintances.’ Either way, friends and acquaintances are both included in social circles, but the strength of our connections with friends is greater than that of acquaintances because friends help each other and that adds time, whereas acquaintances are usually helpful briefly and simply.

Question: My fiancé says it isn’t cruel to kick one’s child out of the house on their eighteenth birthday, for no other reason than, “They are now an adult, and they have to be reliant on themselves.” Is this true?
Answer: I know several families where parents told their teenagers they would be “on their own when they turned eighteen.” It wasn’t a spur-of-the-moment-at-18 announcement, and all had a job and were helped with the financial adjustments of deposits, down payments and furnishings. They were successful. I also know of others who let their legally-adult children loaf around the house while not finding a job, completing schooling or contributing to their own upkeep. Their overage children had “failure to launch” and some failed to accomplish more than being dependent on others or drugs. Now, here’s my approach. We have two sons. We taught them that they never had to lie, cheat or steal to get money. All they had to do was be willing to work and somebody would pay them for it. Our home was heated with burning wood and starting as pre-schoolers, they earned a penny per small pine cone and two pennies for large ones to kindle fires in the heater. The older son lived with us until he graduated college at 22. He worked in maintenance and house painting before graduating, and after, where he is still employed in his 40’s with a six-figure salary. The younger son lived with us until he was 21, working in a paint store and then in construction before enlisting in the USAF. He retired at 42 and was immediately employed as a part-time civilian contractor, and he also has a six-figure income. There is great satisfaction to be gained when we are self-supporting adults, and great comfort and pride in having self-supporting adult children.

Name: Joe Lawson
Question: Why can't we abolish the idea of friendship?
Answer: Merriam-Webster Dictionary defines “abolish” as: “to end the observance or effect of (something, such as a law) : to completely do away with (something),” and “idea” as: ”whatever is known or supposed about something,” and “indefinite or unformed conception.” Therefore, we can only abolish something that is tangibly real, and not ideas about it. For example, a tangible law could prevent me from killing you by abolishing my freedom to do so without punishment, but it cannot stop me from thinking about it.

Question: Is it possible for a person to never be shy at all in their life, even when they were a kid ?

While I do enjoy quiet time alone, I’m also a lifelong extrovert and have been in some form of management or teamwork in the few years when I haven’t been preaching every week as a full-time church pastor. And now, my hobby time is mostly spent relating with people by writing on the Internet, here and for the owner. I have personal online content with over 3 million views, and that ain’t shy.

Question: Is it possible to still be friends with a school friend you haven't seen for years?

Question: How do you start a conversation with a new friend on Facebook?
